verdict.rationale: Marqeta lets users define declarative rules that the platform enforces automatically on transaction events. Velocity controls cap spend amount and frequency over time windows, and authorization controls restrict which merchants a user can spend at. However, the only automatic action evidenced is limiting or declining spend; there is no general event-to-action rules engine. Webhooks and JIT funding hand events to the customer's own system to act on, so they are building blocks rather than product-side automation. Missing for 10: configurable event-triggered actions beyond spend limits (e.g. auto card-state transitions or notifications on rule match), a general rules/automation engine, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
